title: kv-cache: adaptive memory rebalancing and spillover-aware eviction policy
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context and motivation: our KV cache has been repeatedly encountering memory fragmentation and unpredictable paging/spillover events under multimodal workloads and mixed sequence-length traffic. This PR implements an adaptive memory rebalancer and a spillover-aware eviction policy to reduce OOM churn, lower tail latency, and minimize expensive host/disk paging during peak load.

Summary of changes: introduces a background rebalancing worker that monitors per-shard free segments and reclaims fragmented slots via on-device compaction; adds spillover-aware eviction that prefers compactable entries and low-utility shards for paging to host memory; integrates a lightweight scoring function that combines recency, token-count-weight, and fragmentability score to decide eviction/promote order; exposes runtime knobs for per-model memory quotas and async compaction thresholds.

Design details: the rebalancer runs at configurable intervals and does two phases: 1) gentle periodic compaction limited by a device-bound budget (default 2% GPU cycles) that coalesces small free segments into contiguous blocks; 2) emergency defrag triggered when contiguous free memory drops below a threshold or when paging/spillover rate exceeds rate_limit. Compaction is implemented as an atomic swap of contiguous KV pages using the existing page-mapper API to avoid stalling token generation threads.

Eviction policy changes: the new eviction policy is spillover-aware and proceeds in ranked stages: 1) evict entries that are both cold (LRU-ish) and have high fragmentability (i.e., stored as many small fragments) so eviction reduces fragmentation; 2) if host paging permitted, page selected entries to host memory instead of immediate eviction; 3) if neither abates pressure, escalate to disk spillover for very large inactive shards. The scoring function is tunable via config: score = alpha*recency + beta*token_count_penalty + gamma*fragmentability. Default alphas were chosen after offline simulation against production traces.

Scheduling and kernel interactions: the rebalancer coordinates with the continuous batching scheduler to avoid compaction during critical low-latency windows (we respect the scheduler's execution windows). When compaction runs it uses a lightweight kernel path that copies contiguous KV pages using batched DMA-friendly kernels; those kernels were added in runtime/kernels/kv_compact_* and vetted for alignment with existing attention kernel memory model.

API surface and admin controls: runtime config flags added: kv.rebalancer.enabled, kv.rebalancer.interval_ms, kv.rebalancer.budget_pct, kv.eviction.spill_to_host, kv.eviction.spill_to_disk, kv.eviction.score_weights, per-model kv.quota_bytes. Defaults chosen to be conservative; operators can opt-in to aggressive modes. New observability metrics: kv_rebalance_runs_total, kv_compacted_bytes, kv_spilled_to_host_total, kv_spilled_to_disk_total, kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_eviction_score_histogram.

Tests and validation: unit tests for scoring and compaction logic added under runtime/tests/kv_cache_test.cc. Integration tests simulate mixed sequence-length traffic and validate tail-latency behaviour with and without rebalancer. Benchmarks: canary benchmarks show 25-40% reduction in 99th-percentile memory pressure events and 12% improvement in P99 latency for long-sequence workloads. In downstream soak (dedicated canary cluster) we observed a 3x reduction in host-paging incidents over a 48h period.

Commits: see commits list below. CI: initial CI run failed due to a flaky test in continuous-batching integration; test was stabilized and CI re-run which passed.

Files changed (high-level): runtime/kv_cache/{allocator.cc,allocator.h,rebalance.cc,rebalance.h,eviction_policy.cc,eviction_policy.h}, runtime/kernels/kv_compact_kernel.cu, runtime/tests/kv_cache_test.cc, tools/bench/kv_canary_runner.py, docs/kv-cache.md.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: the feature is gated behind kv.rebalancer.enabled=false by default for hosted until we complete staged rollout. For Dedicated/Private customers it is opt-in via the runtime config. No breaking API changes.

Related work: builds on prior eviction heuristics from ENG-6410 and addresses long-tail spillover incidents tracked in SUP-4421.

Release notes: Adds an opt-in KV cache rebalancer and spillover-aware eviction policy to reduce fragmentation and host/disk paging incidents under mixed workloads.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] perf benchmarks, [x] docs update, [x] feature-flag gated for rollout.

review_comments:
Daniel Kim: Please add a safety valve to cap compaction runtime on a single device - we shouldn't allow compaction to starve inference.
Author (Asha): Added rebalancer.budget_pct config and enforced in the worker loop; documented in docs/kv-cache.md.
Priya Rao: The scoring function looks good but can we collect a histogram of fragmentability to tune gamma?
Author: Added kv_fragmentation_ratio metric and a fragmentability histogram; added canary runner to emit telemetry.
Jon Evans: CI failed initially on continuous-batching integration - was this flaky or related?
Author: Flakiness was due to a timing assumption in the integration test; fixed by using scheduler events rather than sleeps. CI was rerun and passed.
release_notes: Opt-in KV cache rebalancer and spillover-aware eviction policy; reduces fragmentation, lowers host/disk paging incidents, improves tail latency under mixed workloads. Feature is disabled by default for hosted environments; configurable knobs and observability metrics included.
tests: unit: runtime/tests/kv_cache_test.cc, integration: tools/bench/kv_canary_runner.py (canary), perf: benchmark lab runs attached. Initial CI: fail (integration flaky) -> fix -> pass.
perf_results: Canary: 12% P99 latency improvement on long-seq workloads; 25-40% reduction in P99 memory pressure events; 3x reduction in host-paging incidents over 48h soak in dedicated canary.
notes: Recommend staged rollout: enable on lower-traffic regions first, monitor kv_spilled_to_host_total and kv_fragmentation_ratio. Backport candidate for the last release branch if validation completes.
